name: Tesslan Wrap Skirt with Tail Slit
description: A knee-length wrap skirt in a loose linen-blend weave, available in deep terracotta and pale sand. The rear panel has a vertical slit that runs 25cm down from the waistband, finished with clean hems on both sides — it parts naturally around a tail and falls back into place at rest. The wrap construction means the waist adjusts freely, accommodating hip geneware variations. Simple, wearable, draws on South Asian wrap traditions.
functionality: Vertical rear slit accommodates tail geneware of varied thickness; wrap waist adjusts for hip geneware variation
what_it_says: You dress with some care and you've found a cut that doesn't treat your geneware as a problem to engineer around.
worn_by: people who prefer skirts to trousers
story_hooks: A character's skirt slit is wider than the standard cut — someone altered it carefully, suggesting a previous owner with an unusually large tail.
The terracotta dye lot is notoriously inconsistent; two people in identical skirts look like they're wearing completely different garments.
